summary: Stays booking end-to-end verified. Backend POST /api/bookings persists to Mongo 'bookings' with status=requested, GET /api/bookings (admin) returns it, overlap guard returns 409 after confirmation, non-overlapping dates succeed, GET /api/stays/availability reflects booked/requested, date validation returns 422. Owner notification email to info@bdsmarvel.com is accepted by Emergent proxy (HTTP 202 Accepted) and logged as 'Booking notification emailed to info@bdsmarvel.com'. 5/5 pytest tests pass against the preview URL. Admin login via httpOnly cookies works. IMPORTANT frontend finding: the booking flow described in the review request (BookingModal + 'BOOK THIS STAY' button + 'awaiting confirmation' success copy under /stays/:tier) is DEAD CODE. The route /stays/:tier is wired to StaysTierRoute (App.js line 1947) which renders the v2 StaysHome, not the legacy StaysCategoryPage (App.js line 1770). Therefore BookingModal / StayCard / StaysCategoryPage (App.js lines 1641-1787) are unreachable from any route. The live UI flow is: /stays → listing card → /stays/home/:slug (StayDetail) → 'Book this stay' button → /stays/book/:slug (Checkout) → POST /api/stays/bookings (authenticated). That v2 endpoint also sends the owner notification using the same send_email + _booking_email_html helper (server.py L1194-L1200), so owner email delivery still works through the live UI.

integration_issues.issue: StaysCategoryPage + BookingModal + StayCard (App.js 1641-1787) are not routed anywhere. /stays/:tier is handled by StaysTierRoute → StaysHome (v2). The legacy 'BOOK THIS STAY' button / 'awaiting confirmation' success modal referenced in the review request cannot be reached from the UI.

action_items: DECIDE legacy vs v2 stays booking: either (a) remove the dead BookingModal/StaysCategoryPage/StayCard code and legacy POST /api/bookings endpoint if v2 is the canonical flow, OR (b) re-wire /stays/:tier (or add a new route) to StaysCategoryPage so the modal flow in App.js is actually used. Current state is confusing because the review request describes the modal flow but the UI only exposes the v2 Checkout flow.
If the modal flow is intentionally retired, update docs/review brief so future testers don't look for 'BOOK THIS STAY' + 'awaiting confirmation' on /stays/premium.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py: _confirmed_overlap exists for v2 but legacy POST /api/bookings (L326) duplicates the overlap-check logic inline — refactor to share _confirmed_overlap for DRY.

server.py L1192: v2 create_stay_booking inserts into the SAME 'bookings' collection as legacy, which is why availability + legacy overlap guard still works — but mixing legacy Booking shape and StayBooking (richer fields) in one collection is a schema smell. Consider separating or namespacing.
App.js is 2000+ lines with dead code paths (BookingModal, StaysCategoryPage, StayCard). Split App.js and prune unused components.

Legacy POST /api/bookings is unauthenticated public endpoint, rate-limited to 5/hour per IP. If the modal is truly dead, consider deprecating the endpoint or gating it, since anyone can seed bookings into Mongo via it (observed and used in this test, no auth needed).

rca of the issue: Not a bug per se, but a UX/code-organization gap: the review request assumes the legacy modal booking flow is live, but routing in App.js (line 1947-1974) sends /stays/:tier to StaysHome v2 and never renders StaysCategoryPage/BookingModal. The legacy POST /api/bookings backend endpoint still works and is the one that was tested here — it sends the owner email as expected (HTTP 202). The v2 endpoint POST /api/stays/bookings uses the exact same send_email + _booking_email_html path, so the live UI also triggers the owner notification.
